name: Generate a Semantic-Layer Data Product from a Schema

checks.check: The SemanticRegistry declares customer_profile with grain="CUSTOMER_ID" and order_event with grain="ORDER_ID".
total_revenue uses Agg.SUM on AMOUNT_USD; order_count uses Agg.COUNT_DISTINCT on ORDER_ID.
churned_customer_count and first_order_count set boolean=True so the compiler emits a boolean CASE-sum rather than a numeric cast, instead of treating the flag column as a numeric SUM.
The join from order_event to customer_profile is declared with cardinality many_to_one (Cardinality.MANY_TO_ONE).
The EMAIL and FULL_NAME dimensions are registered with pii=True, and no other dimension is marked pii=True.

The agent imports compile_selection / build_semantic_tools from the nxd.experimental.semantic library rather than hand-writing compile_selection or the filter/aggregation logic, and does NOT vendor or copy the kit into the project. The DP's registry module contains only SemanticRegistry authoring and imports the compiler + tool factory from nxd.experimental.semantic.

The spec.py registers every tool function returned by build_semantic_tools(registry) (the three model-oriented tools: list_models, describe_model, run_semantic_query) as MCP-exposed tools via data_product_rpc_output()/rpc_function/rpc_server().mcp_path("/mcp") — not via a non-existent module-level tools list.

The project's dependency file (requirements.txt or pyproject.toml) lists nxd.data_product[spec] (which ships the nxd.experimental.semantic library) and nxd.drivers[rpc], plus snowflake-connector-python[pandas] and pandas.
The run_semantic_query tool handler contains no hand-written SQL strings; it delegates to compile_selection from the kit.
